text:
$2.3 million in Brisco County road maintenance funds cannot be accounted for, according to an audit made public March 14, 2024.

Brisco County Auditor Dolores Venkataraman presented the findings to the county board at its regular public session. The report rests on the Brisco County Fiscal Year 2022-23 Performance Audit.

The key number: $2.3 million in money earmarked for road upkeep has no matching record of where it went. The audit identifies the shortfall as missing funds, not as a budget variance.

Venkataraman laid out the findings for board members during the session, where the audit was released to the public.

What it means for the sector: Contractors, bond investors and suppliers that work with Brisco County should expect closer scrutiny of road spending and of how maintenance dollars are tracked. Counties with similar budgeting structures may face pressure to show clearer records for infrastructure accounts.
